chain.label: No university oversight of the donated team-travel flight
chain.trigger: OSU's Flight Department had no records on file regarding the accident pilot, second pilot, or airplane, and the donated flight was not coordinated with the Flight Department Manager

chain.label: Flight in night IMC with no external visual references
chain.trigger: "Instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) prevailed at the time of the accident"; IMC extended from the surface to above the airplane's cruise altitude of 23,000 feet

chain.label: Second pilot had no formal King Air training
chain.trigger: "The second pilot had not received any formal training on King Air airplanes"; he "would have had limited experience with the airplane's systems and emergency procedures"

chain.label: Undetermined single-point defect in the a.c. electrical system
chain.trigger: "one of three components—the inverter selector switch, the inverter select relay, or the avionics inverter select relay—could produce an a.c. power electrical system failure... all three components are potential sources of single-point failures"

chain.label: Complete in-flight loss of a.c. electrical power at 23,200 feet
chain.trigger: "the physical evidence recovered from the wreckage site and the recorded radar data indicate that a complete loss of a.c. electrical power occurred aboard the airplane"

caused_by.evidence: "The Safety Board cannot make a definitive determination regarding what caused the a.c. electrical system to fail"; candidate causes were the inverter select switch/relays or wiring failures, shorts, or opens

chain.label: Pilot-side primary flight instruments flagged and inoperative
chain.trigger: "The complete loss of a.c. electrical power would have rendered most of the pilot's flight instruments inoperative"—altimeter, attitude indicator, HSI, radio altimeter, RMI, altitude preselect; mode C transmission ceased

caused_by.evidence: "if the airplane's a.c. electrical power were lost, flags would appear on most of the instruments on the pilot's (left) side of the cockpit"

chain.label: Pilot prioritized electrical troubleshooting over flying the airplane
chain.trigger: "the pilot did not appropriately manage the workload associated with troubleshooting the loss of a.c. electrical power with the need to establish and maintain positive control of the airplane"

caused_by.evidence: "the pilot would have had salient cues to identify the a.c. electrical power failure"—inverter annunciator, master warning, and instrument flags prompted diagnosis attempts
"because the second pilot had not received any formal King Air training, he would have had limited experience with the airplane's systems and emergency procedures"

chain.label: Pilot failed to fly by reference to the still-working standby instruments
chain.trigger: "the pilot could have safely flown and landed the airplane from the left seat by referencing the available (non-a.c.-powered) flight instruments on the right side of the cockpit"

caused_by.evidence: "the pilot tended to 'lock in on a problem and not fly the airplane.' This observation is consistent with the circumstances of this accident"
"spatial disorientation can only be prevented by visual reference to reliable fixed points on the ground or to flight instruments"—IMC removed all outside references

chain.label: Pilot became spatially disoriented and did not sense the gradual right bank
chain.trigger: "the probable cause of this accident was the pilot's spatial disorientation resulting from his failure to maintain positive manual control of the airplane with the available flight instrumentation"

caused_by.evidence: "The pilot probably did not sense the right descending turn at first because the airplane's bank was entered gradually... he was not able to successfully use the available instruments to regain positive control"
Head movements made while diagnosing the electrical malfunction "might have exacerbated his spatial disorientation" in the absence of outside visual cues

chain.label: Graveyard spiral: 360º right turn, bank over 100º, descent over 15,000 fpm
chain.trigger: "the airplane's estimated flightpath in the final 2 minutes of flight was consistent with a graveyard spiral resulting from pilot spatial disorientation"

caused_by.evidence: "As the airplane's bank angle and descent rate began increasing, the pilot's spatial disorientation most likely persisted"; by 1737:10 pitch exceeded 80º nose down

chain.label: Severe pull-up to arrest the dive at low altitude
chain.trigger: "The pilot likely initiated a severe pull-up maneuver by pulling back on the control column; this action loaded the tail in the downward direction and the wing in the upward direction"

caused_by.evidence: "the pilot attempted to arrest the descent in the final portion of the flight, possibly in response to obtaining visual references of the ground after emerging from the lowest layer of clouds"

chain.label: Aerodynamic overload of the horizontal stabilizer and right outboard wing
chain.trigger: "The pilot input and the airplane reaction required to arrest the descent rate with the available altitude would have placed a large aerodynamic loading on the airplane"

caused_by.evidence: "the aerodynamic loading during the pilot's pull-up maneuver was great enough to overload the horizontal stabilizer downward and the right outboard wing section was sufficiently loaded upward to sustain a permanent bend in the spar"

chain.label: In-flight breakup within several hundred feet of the ground
chain.trigger: "The aerodynamic loading caused the airplane to break apart in flight at a low altitude (within several hundred feet of the ground)"; wreckage spread over 2,800 feet

caused_by.evidence: "the tail structure sections departed the airplane first and... the outboard section of the right wing departed the airplane after the tail sections"

chain.label: Impact with rolling terrain and postcrash fuel-fed fire
chain.trigger: "crashed into rolling terrain near Strasburg, Colorado"; "A fuel-fed fire erupted after the airplane impacted the ground"

caused_by.evidence: "The aerodynamic loading caused the airplane to break apart in flight at a low altitude... and crash into terrain"

chain.label: All 10 occupants fatally injured
chain.trigger: "All 10 occupants aboard N81PF were killed, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire"

caused_by.evidence: "the cause of death for all of the airplane occupants was multiple massive blunt traumatic injuries"; "they were subjected to impact forces that exceeded the limits of human tolerance"
